summary.title: The properties of highly concentrated aqueous CH3COOK/Na binary electrolyte and its use in sodium-ion batteries
summary.authors: Shahid Khalid, Nicolò Pianta, Simone Bonizzoni, Piercarlo Mustarelli, Riccardo Ruffo
summary.executive_summary: This study investigates the physicochemical properties of highly concentrated aqueous binary electrolytes composed of potassium acetate (CH3COOK) and sodium acetate (CH3COONa) for application in sodium-ion batteries. The research addresses the limitations of conventional organic electrolytes, such as safety and cost, and the narrow electrochemical stability window (ESW) of dilute aqueous systems. By maintaining a constant concentration of 20 mol kg-1 CH3COOK and varying CH3COONa from 1 to 7 mol kg-1, the authors characterize thermal, rheological, transport, and electrochemical behaviors. Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) reveals that increasing salt concentration shifts the glass transition temperature (Tg) to higher values, confirming a transition from salt-in-water to water-in-salt (WISE) regimes. The most concentrated solution (7N20K) exhibits a conductivity of 21.2 mS cm-1 at 25°C and an expanded ESW up to 3 V under ideal conditions. To validate the electrolyte's utility, carbon-coated LiTi2(PO4)3 (NASICON) electrodes were tested in the 7N20K solution. The electrode demonstrated reversible Na+ insertion/de-insertion at approximately -0.7 V vs. SHE, achieving a first-cycle anodic capacity of 85 mAh g-1 and 90% capacity retention after 60 cycles. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) indicated excellent interfacial kinetics with a low charge transfer activation energy of 0.12 eV. These findings suggest that acetate-based WISE electrolytes offer a cost-effective, safe, and high-performance alternative for alkaline ion batteries, overcoming the toxicity and cost issues associated with fluorinated salts like LiTFSI.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This study investigates the physicochemical properties of highly concentrated aqueous binary electrolytes composed of potassium acetate (CH3COOK) and sodium acetate (CH3COONa) for application in sodium-ion batteries. The research addresses the limitations of conventional organic electrolytes, such as safety and cost, and the narrow electrochemical stability window (ESW) of dilute aqueous systems. By maintaining a constant concentration of 20 mol kg-1 CH3COOK and varying CH3COONa from 1 to 7 mol kg-1, the authors characterize thermal, rheological, transport, and electrochemical behaviors. Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) reveals that increasing salt concentration shifts the glass transition temperature (Tg) to higher values, confirming a transition from salt-in-water to water-in-salt (WISE) regimes. The most concentrated solution (7N20K) exhibits a conductivity of 21.2 mS cm-1 at 25°C and an expanded ESW up to 3 V under ideal conditions. To validate the electrolyte's utility, carbon-coated LiTi2(PO4)3 (NASICON) electrodes were tested in the 7N20K solution. The electrode demonstrated reversible Na+ insertion/de-insertion at approximately -0.7 V vs. SHE, achieving a first-cycle anodic capacity of 85 mAh g-1 and 90% capacity retention after 60 cycles. Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) indicated excellent interfacial kinetics with a low charge transfer activation energy of 0.12 eV. These findings suggest that acetate-based WISE electrolytes offer a cost-effective, safe, and high-performance alternative for alkaline ion batteries, overcoming the toxicity and cost issues associated with fluorinated salts like LiTFSI.

Research Context
Conventional lithium-ion batteries suffer from safety and cost issues due to organic electrolytes. Aqueous electrolytes are limited by the narrow thermodynamic stability window of water. High-concentration regimes were previously discouraged by ion coupling and rheological limitations. The Water-in-Salt (WISE) concept extends the voltage window by reducing water activity. Fluorinated salts used in WISE have environmental and economic drawbacks. Acetate salts like CH3COOK offer high solubility and low cost for WISE applications.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The study aims to understand the physicochemical properties of CH3COOK/CH3COONa binary solutions. It is hypothesized that high concentrations can extend the electrochemical stability window. The research tests if these solutions can support reversible ion intercalation in NASICON electrodes. The hypothesis is that the most concentrated solution offers the best compromise between transport and stability. The study predicts that Na+ ions will be preferentially inserted due to structural constraints.

Methodological Details
Four electrolyte compositions were prepared with constant 20 mol kg-1 CH3COOK. CH3COONa concentrations varied from 1 to 7 mol kg-1. A 1 M NaAc solution was prepared for comparison. Carbon-coated LiTi2(PO4)3 (CLTP) was synthesized via a one-pot sol-gel route. Precursors included NH4H2PO4, Ti(OC4H9)4, CH3COOLi, and glucose. Calcination was performed at 800°C for 6 hours under argon flux. Thermal analysis used DSC from -120°C to 90°C. Viscosity was measured using a parallel plate rheometer setup. Conductivity was measured via EIS with a dip probe cell. Electrochemical tests used flooded three-electrode cells with glassy carbon electrodes.

Procedures And Architectures
Electrolytes were dissolved in Milli-Q water under sonication. CLTP synthesis involved stirring at 55°C followed by drying at 100°C. XRD analysis was performed using a Rigaku Miniflex 600 with Cu cathode. SEM imaging was conducted using a Zeiss Gemini SEM 450. Viscosity measurements were taken at 10, 20, 30, and 40°C. Conductivity spectra were recorded from 1 Hz to 200 kHz. ESW was estimated using LSV with a 0.1 mA cm-2 threshold. GCPL tests followed a protocol of increasing current rates every 10 cycles. EIS for kinetics was performed from 20°C to 70°C in a Faraday cage. The 1C rate was defined as 136 mA g-1.

Key Results
The glass transition temperature (Tg) increased with salt concentration. The 7N20K solution exhibited a conductivity of 21.2 mS cm-1 at 25°C. The electrochemical stability window reached up to 3 V in ideal conditions. CLTP showed a first-cycle anodic capacity of 85 mAh g-1 in 7N20K. The average charge efficiency was 96% at low current. Capacity retention was 90% after 60 cycles. The activation energy for charge transfer was 0.12 eV. The diffusion coefficient was approximately 10^-13 cm2 s-1 at room temperature. In diluted 1 M NaAc, capacity dropped to 36 mAh g-1 with 40% efficiency. The 7N20K solution followed Kohlrausch's law of strong electrolytes.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The shift in Tg indicates a transition from salt-in-water to water-in-salt regimes. Reduced water activity suppresses hydrogen evolution, expanding the cathodic stability. The electrolyte behaves as a 'structure-making salt' due to strong ion-water interactions. High conductivity at high concentration suggests the formation of water-salt structures. Na+ is preferentially inserted over K+ due to the energy required for K+ accommodation.

Contradictions And Limitations
The ESW estimation may overestimate decomposition limits due to electrode surface area. The study uses 'ideal' conditions which may not reflect practical cell performance. The anodic stability expansion is less significant than the cathodic expansion. The viscosity trend does not follow the Stokes-Einstein equation linearly. The low liquidus temperature is an advantage but requires careful thermal management.

Claims
The 7N20K electrolyte is superior for sodium-ion batteries due to its balance of conductivity and stability. It has a conductivity of 21.2 mS cm-1. It shows a stability window up to 3 V. It supports 90% capacity retention after 60 cycles. The ESW is measured under ideal, small surface area conditions. Conductivity decreases as concentration increases. This enables the development of safe, aqueous alkaline ion batteries.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Ablation was performed by comparing CLTP with pristine LTP. Performance was compared between WISE and diluted 1 M NaAc electrolytes. The carbon coating was essential for good electrochemical performance.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows DSC curves indicating Tg shifts with concentration. Figure 2 displays ionic conductivity vs. temperature following VTF behavior. Figure 3 shows viscosity measurements following Arrhenius behavior. Figure 4 presents Walden plots classifying electrolytes as quasi-ideal. Figure 5 shows LSV profiles for electrochemical stability windows. Figure 7 compares potential profiles in WISE vs. diluted electrolytes. Figure 8 shows impedance spectra with depressed semicircles. Figure 9 presents the Arrhenius plot of charge transfer resistance.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the characterization of a high-concentration acetate WISE electrolyte. 2. The strongest evidence is the 90% capacity retention and 3 V stability window. 3. The future path is the development of practical alkaline ion batteries using this electrolyte.
